artworks.title: The Farnese Bull
artworks.artist: Apollonius of Tralles and Tauriscus of Tralles (Roman copy)
artworks.year: c. 2nd century BC (original); Roman Imperial copy
artworks.description: The monumental Naples marble: Zethus and Amphion bind Dirce to the bull — Hellenistic pathos for the Theban twins' revenge, the largest ancient sculpture group to survive.

artworks.title: Zethus and Amphion Binding Dirce
artworks.description: Rijksmuseum engraving of the Farnese subject: Zethus named in the title as he and Amphion lash Dirce to the horns — print culture spreading the bull revenge.

artworks.title: Zethus and Amphion
artworks.description: Troschel's Neue Pinakothek sculpture: the Theban twins as nineteenth-century marble — Zethus the strong builder beside Amphion the lyre.

artworks.title: Punishment of Dirce (pelike)
artworks.description: Lucanian pelike in Policoro: Dirce's punishment with the twins present — South Italian vase-painting of the myth the Farnese Bull later monumentalized.

artworks.title: Amphion and Zethus (Yusupov Palace)
artworks.description: Decorative pair in the Yusupov Palace, Saint Petersburg: Amphion and Zethus as twin founders — Zethus the strength that raised Thebes' walls.

popCulture.title: Farnese Bull
popCulture.description: The Naples colossal group — Zethus and Amphion's revenge on Dirce — remains the twins' defining afterlife in stone.

popCulture.title: Amphion and Zethus
popCulture.description: Sons of Antiope who built Thebes — Amphion with the lyre, Zethus with raw strength.
